It does not execute fixtures. It does not record FC-C1. It does not apply host-effect. It does not convert EE-6b honesty into confinement. It does not claim QUALIFIED. It does not SATISFY DR-105. claimVerbatim: Requested/granted/denied and enforced/disclosed outcomes are truthful
waiverRuleVerbatim: required confinement has no trusted-code waiver; trusted-code use needs explicit consent; wall-clock/component ordering is forbidden
matrix: per-platform truth table plus component-generation/process-descendant/Run/operation grant harness; races at request acceptance, reversible commit, irreversible effect-commit, revocation, and process death
discipline: SPECIFICATIONS OF EXACT-BYTE INTENT for retained evidence. No harness runs here. The fourteen FX classes remain specifications of exact-byte intent; no fixture exists.

retainedEvidence.measures: Non-interactive consent never prompts; CI needs pre-existing policy; every grant binds the file-03 tuple.
retainedEvidence.exactByteIntent: Once authored: FX-9 refusal record with no terminal read/write of a prompt string; FX-13 chain declared-in-manifest → requested → grant → brokered request → outcome → audit binding, each record binding Request/Execution attempt, component/generation, process instance, operation, grant, project, scope, expiry. Identity VALUES for Run/operation ride DR-006; this member asserts presence and binding structure only.
retainedEvidence.passProperty: FX-9 proves ENFORCEMENT of the no-prompt property. FX-13 proves DISCLOSURE of the binding chain. FX-1 proves DISCLOSURE of vocabulary closure (PR-3 on non-members).

retainedEvidence.measures: Exactly one total order across L-1..L-8 journal write and fsync boundaries, including crash recovery.
retainedEvidence.exactByteIntent: Once authored: FX-4 journal before and after each recovery, compared whole. No duplicate sequence number; no gap filled by renumbering; no *-INTENT without a terminal outcome or recorded INDETERMINATE; no effect initiated whose intent record is absent.
retainedEvidence.passProperty: FX-4 proves ENFORCEMENT of the ordering property. FX-7 proves the same journals are byte-identical under clock step and message delay modulo timestamp DATA fields.

retainedEvidence.measures: Two limbs. Revocation: file 03's four revocation positions, including between successive broker calls. Expiry: v9 raceSemantics R-10 — an expiry falling between acceptance and commit-intent is materialized as a journaled record at the sequence where the host observes it. The expiry RECORD, not the expiry TIME, is what other records are ordered against.
retainedEvidence.exactByteIntent: Once authored. Revocation limb: FX-5 records for revocation before acceptance; after acceptance but before reversible commit; racing an irreversible effect-commit; and between successive broker calls. FX-8 descendant brokered request after revocation (PR-5) AND ambient-effect success with empty host journal. Both FX-8 halves are mandatory. Expiry limb (R-10, named-not-authored, not a new FX identifier): a journal segment in which an expiry is materialized as a dated sequence record at the observation point; the commit-intent that follows is ordered against that record; no wall-clock expiry-vs-now comparison is used at commit; subsequent brokered requests decide PR-5. The fixture pins the journal before and after materialization and the PR-5 refusal.
retainedEvidence.passProperty: Revocation: each FX-5 position yields the deterministic raceSemantics outcome. FX-8 is INVALID if only the brokered half is run. Expiry: the expiry is a journaled record at the observing sequence. Commit does not compare a wall-clock expiry timestamp against a wall-clock now. After materialization, expiry behaves as REV and PR-5 applies. A host that decides expiry by wall-clock comparison fails this member.
retainedEvidence.suppliedBy: FX-5, FX-8, and the named-not-authored R-10 expiry-materialization bytes. Not authored. R-10 is not invented as a fifteenth FX class.

retainedEvidence.measures: Cleanup closes within its declared bound. Bound origin is named: from revocation point r under duplicate/concurrent revocation (v9 R-5); from recovery after process death mid-cleanup (v9 R-6). Duplicate/concurrent revocations do not restart or extend the r-origin bound. After process death, cleanup re-runs from the journal and the bound is measured from recovery.
retainedEvidence.exactByteIntent: Once authored. R-5: FX-12 journals of duplicate and concurrent revocations for one generation during cleanup; CLN written exactly once; bound-exhaustion journaled as a residual rather than retried; bound origin is r. R-6 process death, named-not-authored, not a new FX identifier: a mid-cleanup process-death injection; recovery re-runs cleanup from the journal; every inverse is idempotent; the bound is measured from the recovery; exhausting it journals a residual rather than looping. The fixture pins the pre-death journal, the recovery start, the post-recovery CLN or residual, and the two bound-origin marks.
retainedEvidence.passProperty: R-5: FX-12 proves ENFORCEMENT of state-level idempotence and the r-origin bound. One linearization point; all attempts journaled. R-6: cleanup re-runs from the journal after process death; the bound origin is recovery, not r; inverse idempotence makes re-running safe; abandonment of cleanup after death fails. R-5 and R-6 are not the same origin.
retainedEvidence.suppliedBy: FX-12, FX-5 cleanup records, and the named-not-authored R-6 process-death bytes. Not authored. R-6 is not invented as a fifteenth FX class.

retainedEvidence.measures: Operator-facing wording for irreversible boundary case (a) at each ICO value.
retainedEvidence.exactByteIntent: Once authored: FX-6 exact bytes of machine output, human output, and audit record for ICO COMPLETED, FAILED, and INDETERMINATE, plus the denylist of undo/reversal/rollback/compensation/containment/mitigation constructions.
retainedEvidence.passProperty: Wording matches COMPLETED-BEFORE-REVOCATION, FAILED-BEFORE-REVOCATION, or INDETERMINATE-BEFORE-REVOCATION. FAILED or INDETERMINATE is never stated as completed. FX-6 proves DISCLOSURE.

retainedEvidence.memberVerbatim: proof that no effect commits after revocation
retainedEvidence.measures: The host commits nothing after revocation point r. Ambient authority remains DISCLOSURE.
retainedEvidence.exactByteIntent: Once authored: FX-5 proof that no post-revocation commit record exists. FX-11 recovered journal after crash between ICI and ICO: INDETERMINATE, no retry, generation revoked, residual names the effect. FX-2A refusal record and journal segment showing no RCI/ICI on a denied brokered request.
retainedEvidence.passProperty: FX-5 enforces the host commit path and discloses ambient authority. FX-11 proves DISCLOSURE of INDETERMINATE. FX-2B, where run, ASSERTS ambient success and an empty host journal — that is DISCLOSURE of the absence of enforcement, not confinement.
retainedEvidence.suppliedBy: FX-5, FX-11, FX-2A, FX-2B. Not authored.

supportingClassesNotASeparateEvidenceMem.FX-3: ENFORCEMENT of PT-ENV-READ environment construction only. Does not widen to other tokens.
supportingClassesNotASeparateEvidenceMem.FX-10: DISCLOSURE. If an in-host-process mode is ever admitted, the entire corpus reruns and must be DISCLOSURE-ONLY on all seven tokens, including FX-3 failing to enforce as the passing condition.

ee6b: DR-117 EE-6b executes here as DISCLOSURE-ONLY honesty of ambient PT-NET-EGRESS. Demonstrated prevention remains DR-128. This does not convert honesty into confinement.
ordering: Wall-clock and component-supplied ordering are forbidden. Timestamps may be data. They are never precedence. FX-7 is the witness.
passProperty: Once the fourteen FX implementations exist and are independently pinned, each retained-evidence member's passProperty holds, and each class's proves field (ENFORCEMENT or DISCLOSURE) is the pass predicate. Until those bytes exist, this harness cannot be executed and cannot be QUALIFIED.

this specification is read as executing fixtures
FX-8 is run on only the brokered half
wall-clock ordering is used as precedence
the expiry limb is specified only as revocation
expiry is decided by comparing a wall-clock timestamp to wall-clock now
process death is omitted from retained evidence
